introduction.text: The Basilica di Santa Prassede is an early‑medieval church in Rome that houses some of the city’s oldest mosaics and important relics, making it a key monument in the history of Christian art and architecture.

history.description: Pope St. Evaristus founded the Titulus S. Praxedis around 112.
The church’s origins date to at least the fifth century, when a Christian community was established on the site.
Pope Hadrian I commissioned the current church around 780 to house the relics of St. Praxedes and St. Pudentiana.
Pope Paschal I enlarged and decorated the basilica around 828.
Alfred the Great visited Rome around 855‑856 and was impressed by the basilica’s beauty.
Since 1198 the Vallombrosian monks have maintained the basilica.
In 1223 a relic of the column of the Flagellation was brought to the basilica by Cardinal Giovanni Colonna.

design.description: The basilica’s interior is dominated by a mosaic program in the apse, apsidal arch and triumphal arch, created by a team of professional mosaicists under Pope Paschal I.
A column believed to be part of the Flagellation of Christ is housed in the basilica, allegedly discovered by Helena in the early fourth century.
The basilica’s layout follows a traditional Roman church plan with a central nave, transept and a prominent triumphal arch.

art.description: The main altarpiece, a canvas of St. Praxedes gathering the blood of the martyrs (c. 1730‑35), was painted by Domenico Muratori.
A portrait of Cardinal Angelo Maria Querini (1747) by Jacopo Zoboli adorns the right column of the triumphal arch.
An Annunciation by Stefano Pieri is displayed within the basilica.
